questions.prompt: Production and staging use different database connection strings, and each must remain attached to its environment during a slot swap. What should be configured?

options.text: Mark the connection strings as deployment slot settings.
options.explanation: Sticky connection strings remain associated with their slot.

options.text: Leave them swappable and rely on different display names.
options.explanation: Display names do not prevent connection string swapping.

options.text: Put both connection strings only in the shared plan name.
options.explanation: The plan name does not supply environment-specific application configuration.

options.text: Change only the staging traffic percentage.
options.explanation: Traffic routing does not make connection strings sticky.

questions.prompt: Which App Service configuration remains with its slot during a swap?

options.explanation: Managed identities are listed among settings that do not swap.
Content is the main item moved between slots.
App settings can swap unless configured sticky or subject to documented exceptions.
Framework settings are among the swappable configuration items.

questions.prompt: A release is swapped from staging to production and performs an external database schema migration. What does swapping the slots back provide?

options.text: A code/configuration rollback path that still needs a separate database compatibility or recovery plan.
options.explanation: A slot swap does not undo external database mutations.

options.text: Automatic reversal of every database change.
options.explanation: External data is outside the slot content swap.

options.text: Automatic restoration of all production data from Azure Backup.
options.explanation: Swap does not trigger database restoration.

options.text: Deletion of the newer database schema with guaranteed zero data loss.
options.explanation: A swap has no such schema or data-loss guarantee.
